claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 12356 - National Security Information (2 April 1982)
claims.text: IT DID NOT REVOKE EO 11652, and the claim that it did is wrong. EO 12065 had already revoked 11652 in 1978. Also note that the Federation of American Scientists URL usually given for this order, irp.fas.org/offdocs/eo/eo-12356.htm, returns HTTP 404 and does not exist.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 12356 - National Security Information (2 April 1982)
claims.text: Section 1.1(c) resolves doubt toward secrecy: where there is reasonable doubt about the level, the information is to be safeguarded at the higher level.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 12356 - National Security Information (2 April 1982)
claims.sourceText: EO 12356 full text term searches, against EO 12065 sec. 3-303, https://www.archives.gov/federal-register/codification/executive-order/12356.html and https://irp.fas.org/offdocs/eo/eo-12065.htm
claims.text: THE PUBLIC-INTEREST TEST IS GONE, AND THIS WAS CHECKED FROM BOTH SIDES. The phrase 'public interest' occurs zero times in EO 12356, as does any form of 'balanc'. Its predecessor EO 12065 had required at section 3-303 that an official 'determine whether the public interest in disclosure outweighs the damage to national security'. The obligation to weigh disclosure against harm was removed in 1982 and has not returned.

claims.nodeLabel: Executive Order 12356 - National Security Information (2 April 1982)
claims.text: RECLASSIFICATION AFTER DISCLOSURE IS EXPRESSLY AUTHORISED. Section 1.6(c) permits officials to 'reclassify information previously declassified and disclosed if it is determined in writing' that it requires protection and 'may reasonably be recovered'. Section 1.6(d) permits classification or reclassification AFTER an agency has received a request under the Freedom of Information Act, the Privacy Act or the mandatory review provisions, on a document-by-document basis.
